stories.title: Daisy and the Tune with Two Makers
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: Giving someone credit helps them feel their work belongs.
moralRhyme: Say who helped the tune along,
Two friends helped to make our song!

youtube.title: Daisy and the Tune with Two Makers | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Squeaks stopped tapping during Daisy's new tune. Daisy looked down at the suddenly quiet bench. A gentle friendship story. Giving someone credit helps them feel their work belongs. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Squeaks stopped tapping during Daisy's new tune.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Daisy looked down at the suddenly quiet bench.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Why has our little rhythm disappeared?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You told everyone you made the whole thing.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy wanted to present a tune at their picnic.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She had made a cheerful three-note melody.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I worked hard on those three happy notes.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And I made the tapping pattern underneath them.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy sang her part without Squeaks's taps.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The pauses felt longer than she remembered.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My melody seems to have lost its little feet.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Those little feet were the rhythm I brought.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy tried tapping while singing both parts.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her wings rushed ahead of the last note.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I can do everything if I practice faster.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: That is not what made me feel left out.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Who made the little tapping part?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Daisy stopped and listened to the quiet bench.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Squeaks held her tiny tapping sticks still.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Was it because you wanted a louder tapping turn?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: It was because my part sounded like it belonged to nobody.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy offered to call the tune a picnic tune.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Squeaks looked at the unnamed little rhythm picture.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That name says where we will play it.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: But it still does not say who made our parts.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy thought about their first practice together.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Squeaks had invented the taps before the melody settled.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You made the beat that helped my notes fit.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And you made the notes that gave my beat a home.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy changed the words of her introduction.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She pointed to both friends on their little poster.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Melody by Daisy. Tapping rhythm by Squeaks.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: That introduction has a place for both of us.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They practiced the beginning without rushing anything.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Daisy waited for Squeaks's first little tap.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your rhythm can tell my melody when to start.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then I shall give it a very clear welcome.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Can Daisy name both makers?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Squeaks tapped and Daisy sang their short melody.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The two parts fitted around the same gentle pauses.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: There are our little musical feet again!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And nobody has to hide behind the notes.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Daisy invited Squeaks to stand beside the poster.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: She tried the new introduction before their picnic.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: We made this tune together, with two different parts.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I am ready to play my part with yours.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They performed for their pretend picnic audience.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Daisy named both makers before beginning the tune.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Please listen for Squeaks's wonderful tapping rhythm.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And Daisy's three cheerful notes above it.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Their final note ended on Squeaks's final tap.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Daisy offered her friend a warm little bow.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Thank you for telling me what I missed.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Thank you for making room for my work.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They put both names beneath the little music picture.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The tapping sticks rested beside Daisy's notes.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Our tune has two makers and one happy ending.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And a very small mouse with properly introduced feet.
lines.speaker: friend
